finalText:
**Issue #29 — Earlier chats list clips away the time and waiting count.** Committed as `ad50a19` on `uf/usagefoundry-19-2514d080`.

## What changed

`src/app/chat/page.tsx:303-327` only — the one `<button>` per row in the "Earlier chats" list. It was one `truncate`d line holding title *and* metadata; it is now two lines inside the same button: a `block truncate` span for the title, and a `mt-0.5 flex flex-wrap items-center gap-1.5 text-2xs text-ink-faint` span carrying `fmtRelative(c.updatedAt)` and, when `pendingCount > 0`, `<Badge tone="accent">{n} waiting</Badge>` — the same badge the Proposals card heading already uses for the same phrase. `title={c.title ?? "Untitled"}` on the button, matching `RunCard.tsx:100/121` and `branches/page.tsx:408`.

No `aria-label`: the full title is in the DOM (clipped visually only), so a screen reader already reads it, and an `aria-label` would *replace* the accessible name and hide the "N waiting" text from assistive tech. `title` supplies the hover string and the accessible description.

One README bullet added to *Not yet verified by hand*, because this is a layout change no browser here has rendered.

## Acceptance criteria

- **Time and waiting count visible with an 80-character title** — met structurally: `overflow:hidden;white-space:nowrap` is now scoped to a span containing only the title, and the metadata is a sibling below it with no clipping ancestor (the Card sets no `overflow`), so nothing can eat it regardless of title length. Its own content is short — `fmtRelative` emits `12m ago`/`1h 30m ago`, plus a ~90px badge, against ~328px of content width — and `flex-wrap` handles the worst case. Not measured in a browser; see below.
- **Full title on hover and to assistive technology** — `title` attribute carries the untruncated string; the text node is complete in the DOM.
- **Pending proposals identifiable from the list** — the accent badge on the metadata line.
- **Holds at the narrow breakpoint** — the row is a stretched flex item, so at one column the title simply truncates later; nothing else changes.

## Verification

```
NODE_ENV=development npm ci --include=dev   → ok
npm run typecheck                            → clean
npm test                                     → 220 pass / 0 fail (37 suites)
npm run build                                → fails: TypeError: generate is not a function
env -u __NEXT_PRIVATE_STANDALONE_CONFIG npx next build → succeeds, /chat prerendered
```

The bare `npm run build` failure is **pre-existing and environmental, not caused by this change** — it reproduces identically with the change stashed. I traced it: this container exports `__NEXT_PRIVATE_STANDALONE_CONFIG` (leaked in from the standalone server it runs under), and `next/dist/server/config.js:1032` short-circuits to `JSON.parse` of it, which drops every function-valued key — so `config.generateBuildId` is `undefined` and `generateBuildId()` at `next/dist/build/index.js:358` throws. Unsetting that one variable makes the build pass. The README already carries a bullet claiming `next build` "could not be run here at all"; I left that bullet alone (it belongs to another change's paragraph) but the workaround above is the answer to it.

I also grepped the built stylesheet to confirm the utilities I used actually compiled rather than silently emitting nothing (the failure mode `CLAUDE.md` warns about for Tailwind): `.truncate`, `.block`, `.mt-0\.5`, `.flex-wrap`, `.gap-1\.5`, `.text-2xs`, `.items-center`, `.text-ink-faint` are all present in `.next/static/css/c0398e2ceec0e54f.css` with the expected declarations.

**What I could not verify:** no browser in this container, so nothing pixel-level — that the metadata line is legible at 360px, and how the two-line rows read against the 6px inter-row gap. The exact check a human should run: `docker compose up --build`, open `/chat` with three or more chats whose first messages are 60+ characters, one of them with pending proposals.

**No regression test.** The issue does not ask for one, and the repo's rendering-test idiom (`renderToStaticMarkup` over a component) cannot reach this markup: it is inline in a page component whose hooks and `fetch` mean `chats.length > 1` is never true at render time, and extracting it would restructure a file five other branches must land on — explicitly out of bounds for this run. `npm test` was run only to confirm nothing broke.

**Noticed, left alone:** the `Decided` list two cards above (`page.tsx:280-292`) has the same unbounded-title shape — a `p.title` with no truncation and no `title` attribute — but it wraps rather than clips, so it is a different defect and not this issue's.

DONE
